blocking_findings.location: backend/src/main/java/dev/allow/backend/DocumentWorker.java execute process-start identity catch and recovery
blocking_findings.finding: After launcher.launch succeeds, pid is assigned before ProcessIdentity.startTicks. If the child exits immediately and /proc disappears before that read, the IOException catch kills/waits and throws outside the subsequent finally that sets reaped. Thus reaped remains false and startTicks null. DocumentAttempt is marked finished, but every same-process retry invokes recovery(), which permanently throws Reaping is not established. The durable reservation/nonce remains unavailable until whole server restart. If waitFor itself is interrupted in that catch, unconditional reaping is additionally not guaranteed.
blocking_findings.trigger: Immediate sandbox/startup failure or injected ProcessIdentity.startTicks IOException after child creation. No parser-validity assumption is needed. Existing worker constructor/prelaunch failure tests do not cover this interval.
blocking_findings.resolution: Put every successfully created child under unconditional uninterruptible-reap cleanup immediately. Preserve a trusted, explicit confirmed-exit-before-start-identity recovery state supported by the narrow bridge, or obtain stable process identity atomically enough that all started-child failures have usable recovery evidence. Do not label an actually started process noWorkerStarted. Add a focused startup-identity-failure and interrupted-cleanup regression proving subsequent same-key retry can rotate/recover and the child cannot survive permit release.
blocking_findings.scope: Availability/resource-ownership edge; no wrong accepted artifact or unauthorized SQL write demonstrated. A full server restart currently provides recovery, but ordinary retry remains stuck.
